hook: SCP-343 is the Foundation's file on a friendly old man who says he made the universe and can more or less prove it. It is short, warm, and a little sly. Read the addenda carefully, since the interesting part happens in what goes missing.
whyItMatters: It is one of the most widely read early entries, and a natural starting point for thinking about how the site handles gods. Rather than a threat, it offers an all-powerful being who mostly wants company, which makes containment a polite fiction. The alleged-god tag it carries groups it with many other claimed deities, and this one stands out for how little it asks of anyone.
thingsToNotice:
The containment procedures are almost a joke on themselves: the Foundation simply admits it cannot hold him and settles for keeping him supplied and visited. The reported effects on staff, from better mood to fewer deaths, read like quiet blessings filed as anomalies.

The later addenda hint at a person who tried to treat him as an interrogation target and then seems to have been erased from the records. The article never states what happened, and leaving that gap unfilled is what gives the cozy surface its edge.

related.note: Another entity whose main effect is making staff feel better.
A charming talker whose grand claims the Foundation cannot quite verify.
